Seminar Title:

Assessment of whole-body vibrations in dumper operators in eastern India

Abstract:

In the opencast mines, dumper operators usually suffer from Whole Body Vibration (WBV) exposure. Dumpers used in the opencast mines for the production of raw minerals produce a high intensity of vibrations, which are transmitted throughout the body of the worker from vibrating surfaces. WBV exposure levels correlate with escalating health risks for operators, classified by ISO 2631-1 into minimal, moderate, and high categories based on daily Root Mean Squared (RMS) acceleration (m/s2) A(8) or Vibration Dose Value VDV (8). The health impact include fatigue, motion sickness, prolonged exposure increases the deterioration of the nervous system, circulatory system, digestive system of the worker. These risks manifest progressively from discomfort to chronic disorders, especially low back pain and spinal issues in mining contexts. The main aim of the project is to measure the WBV exposure of various dumper operators in opencast mines in India and to study how machine condition, haul road condition, operational culture and personal factors influence vibration exposure of mine operators in an opencast mine. The tri-axial accelerometer instrument was mounted on the seat pan of the dumper, for which the WBV was to be measured, and the operator was asked to sit over the instrument properly as described in ISO 2631-1:1997. Then, by following the ISO 2631-1:1997 standards, RMS and VDV were measured. The instrument used for the measurement of WBV was SV 106A. A total of 18 dumper operators were selected from an opencast iron ore mine in eastern India. It was found that for RMS measurement, about 33.33 % of the operators were exposed to WBV above the Exposure Limit Value, about 38.88 % were exposed to WBV within the Exposure Action Value and Exposure Limit Value, and the remaining were exposed to WBV below the Exposure Action Value. Using Pearson correlation and multivariate regression analysis, it is found that the potential predictors were the age of the operator and the age of the machine
